quests.instruction: Touch the tool with soft bristles that spreads paint onto our paper!
quests.question: Paintbrush
quests.hint: It has a long handle and soft bristles on one end.
quests.explanation: Yes! A paintbrush spreads paint smoothly across our paper.
quests.funFact: Paintbrush bristles can be made from soft animal hair or from nylon!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the room where your class learns together!
quests.question: Classroom
quests.hint: This room has desks, chairs, and a board at the front.
quests.explanation: Yes! A classroom is the room where you learn together with your teacher.
quests.funFact: Classrooms around the world can look very different, but they are all places to learn!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for a person who comes to school to learn!
quests.question: Student
quests.hint: This person carries a backpack and sits at a desk to learn.
quests.explanation: Yes! A student is a person who goes to school to learn new things.
quests.funFact: Students all around the world go to school to learn new things every day!

quests.instruction: Touch the school word for the person who teaches your class every day!
quests.question: Teacher
quests.hint: This person stands at the front of the classroom most of the day.
quests.explanation: Yes! A teacher is the person who helps students learn every day.
quests.funFact: Teachers often spend extra time planning fun lessons for their whole class!

quests.instruction: Touch the pen with bright, bold ink that we use for coloring!
quests.question: Marker
quests.hint: It has a cap you must remember to put back on.
quests.explanation: Yes! A marker draws bold, colorful lines on paper or a whiteboard.
quests.funFact: Markers can dry out if you forget to put the cap back on!

quests.instruction: Touch the thin, flat sheet that we write and draw on every day!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: It is thin, flat, and usually white or another light color.
quests.explanation: Yes! Paper is the flat sheet we write, draw, and color on.
quests.funFact: Paper was first made from tree bark, plants, and old cloth long ago!

quests.instruction: Touch the flat holder that keeps our loose papers from getting lost!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It opens and closes like a thin book made of paper or plastic.
quests.explanation: Yes! A folder holds loose papers safely so they do not get lost or bent.
quests.funFact: Some folders have pockets on both sides to sort different papers!

quests.instruction: Touch the container we pack with food to eat at school!
quests.question: Lunchbox
quests.hint: You open it at lunchtime to find your sandwich or snack inside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A lunchbox carries our food safely to school until it's time to eat.
quests.funFact: Some lunchboxes have special cool packs inside to keep food fresh and cold!

quests.instruction: Find the item that comes in a big stack, ready for writing!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: A pencil, crayon, or marker leaves its mark right on this.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use paper for writing letters and drawing pictures.
quests.funFact: Most paper today is made from trees that are grown just for that purpose!

quests.instruction: Find the item we slide our worksheets inside to keep them safe!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It has no pages of its own, but it holds other papers inside.
quests.explanation: That's right! We slide our worksheets into a folder to keep them tidy.
quests.funFact: Colorful folders can help students quickly find the right subject for each class!

quests.instruction: Touch the small tool that rubs pencil marks away from your paper!
quests.question: Eraser
quests.hint: Rub it gently over a pencil mark and watch it disappear.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use an eraser to clean up little writing mistakes.
quests.funFact: Before rubber erasers, people used soft bread to rub out pencil marks!

quests.instruction: Find the box we open at lunchtime to eat our sandwich or fruit!
quests.question: Lunchbox
quests.hint: It keeps your food safe on the way to school.
quests.explanation: That's right! We open a lunchbox at lunchtime to enjoy our food.
quests.funFact: Packing your own lunchbox can be a fun way to choose your favorite foods!

quests.instruction: Find the word for someone who sits in class and does homework!
quests.question: Student
quests.hint: This word describes you every single day that you go to school.
quests.explanation: That's right! A student sits in class, listens, and practices new skills.
quests.funFact: Being a good student means trying your best, even when something feels hard!

quests.instruction: Find the word for the room with desks, a board, and your teacher!
quests.question: Classroom
quests.hint: Your teacher and your classmates spend most of the day here with you.
quests.explanation: That's right! A classroom has desks, chairs, and a board for lessons.
quests.funFact: Some classrooms have cozy reading corners with soft cushions for story time!

quests.instruction: Touch the school tool we use to write letters and draw pictures!
quests.question: Pencil
quests.hint: It often has an eraser sitting right on top of it!
quests.explanation: That's right! We hold a pencil to make letters and pictures on paper.
quests.funFact: Long ago, people wrote with sticks and feathers before pencils were invented!

quests.instruction: Find the tool that makes paper sticky so two pieces join together!
quests.question: Glue Stick
quests.hint: It helps two pieces of paper stay joined together, like magic!
quests.explanation: That's right! We twist up a glue stick and rub it onto paper to stick things.
quests.funFact: A glue stick dries clear, so you can barely see it on your paper!

quests.instruction: Find the tool that draws thick, colorful lines on paper or a board!
quests.question: Marker
quests.hint: Its ink is thick and bold, much darker than a pencil's line.
quests.explanation: That's right! We use a marker for bright writing and drawing.
quests.funFact: Some markers even smell like fruit, such as strawberry or grape!

quests.instruction: Find the tool we dip into paint before we brush it onto paper!
quests.question: Paintbrush
quests.hint: You dip its bristles into paint before brushing it onto paper.
quests.explanation: That's right! We dip a paintbrush in paint before we brush a picture.
quests.funFact: Artists use paintbrushes in many sizes, from tiny tips to big, wide ones!

quests.instruction: Find the bag that holds your books safely on the walk to school!
quests.question: Backpack
quests.hint: You pack it in the morning and open it again after school.
quests.explanation: That's right! We wear a backpack on our shoulders to carry our things.
quests.funFact: Some backpacks have a special pocket just the right size for a water bottle!

quests.instruction: Touch the word for the person carrying a backpack full of books to class!
quests.question: Student
quests.hint: This person listens to the teacher and practices new skills.
quests.explanation: Well done! Every child in a classroom is a student, just like you.
quests.funFact: Students all around the world go to school to learn new things every day!

quests.instruction: Find the person who helps students learn to read, write, and count!
quests.question: Teacher
quests.hint: You raise your hand when you have a question for this person.
quests.explanation: That's right! A teacher explains new lessons and answers our questions.
quests.funFact: A single teacher can help hundreds of students learn over many years!

quests.instruction: Touch the container that keeps our snacks safe until lunchtime!
quests.question: Lunchbox
quests.hint: It usually has a lid or a zipper to keep food fresh.
quests.explanation: Well done! A lunchbox keeps a sandwich, fruit, or snack fresh and safe.
quests.funFact: Some lunchboxes have special cool packs inside to keep food fresh and cold!

quests.instruction: Touch the thin sheet a pencil or crayon can leave a mark on!
quests.question: Paper
quests.hint: You can fold it, cut it, or draw on it in class.
quests.explanation: Well done! Paper is ready for a pencil, crayon, or marker to color it.
quests.funFact: Paper was first made from tree bark, plants, and old cloth long ago!

quests.instruction: Find the piece of furniture where we write and stack our books!
quests.question: Desk
quests.hint: You place your notebook and pencil on it before you start writing.
quests.explanation: That's right! We keep our books and pencils on our desk in class.
quests.funFact: The word desk comes from an old word meaning a table for writing!

quests.instruction: Touch the item that closes like a book to protect our papers!
quests.question: Folder
quests.hint: It keeps your worksheets flat and safe inside your backpack.
quests.explanation: Well done! A folder protects our papers on the way to and from school.
quests.funFact: Some folders have pockets on both sides to sort different papers!

quests.instruction: Find the tool that snips paper into new shapes when you squeeze it!
quests.question: Scissors
quests.hint: It is always used slowly and carefully, with an adult nearby to help.
quests.explanation: That's right! We squeeze the handles of scissors to cut along a line.
quests.funFact: School scissors often have rounded tips to help keep little fingers safe!

quests.instruction: Find the soft tool that fixes a mistake without tearing your paper!
quests.question: Eraser
quests.hint: It never works on pen marks, only on pencil marks.
quests.explanation: Well done! An eraser helps keep your paper neat and tidy.
quests.funFact: Erasers are made from rubber, which is why they can bend and squish!

quests.instruction: Find the seat with four legs that we sit on in class!
quests.question: Chair
quests.hint: Every desk in the classroom has one sitting right next to it.
quests.explanation: That's right! We sit on a chair while we work at our desk.
quests.funFact: Some classroom chairs are stacked together and stored when they're not needed!

quests.instruction: Touch the tool that needs its lid closed so it will not dry out!
quests.question: Marker
quests.hint: If you leave its cap off too long, it can dry out.
quests.explanation: Well done! A marker's ink is thicker and darker than a pencil's.
quests.funFact: Markers can dry out if you forget to put the cap back on!

quests.instruction: Find the small pouch we zip our pencils and crayons inside!
quests.question: Pencil Case
quests.hint: It holds your pencils, eraser, and ruler all in one place.
quests.explanation: That's right! We zip our writing tools safely inside a pencil case.
quests.funFact: A tidy pencil case can help you find your pencil in just one second!
